questions.enonce_markdown:
Enumerate seven (7) reasons for food preservation.

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Seven reasons for preserving food (1 mark each):

1. To **prevent spoilage** of food by micro-organisms (bacteria, moulds, yeasts) and by enzymes.
2. To **keep food for a longer time** (to lengthen its shelf life).
3. To **have foods out of season**, all the year round.
4. To **store the surplus** when food is plentiful and cheap, for the time of scarcity.
5. To **avoid waste** of food and so save money.
6. To **prevent food poisoning** and keep food safe to eat.
7. To **keep the nutritive value, flavour and appearance** of the food, and to make it possible to **transport it over long distances** and to add variety to the diet.

questions.enonce_markdown:
State five (5) points to consider when selecting beverages.

(5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Five points to consider when selecting beverages (1 mark each):

1. **Cost**: the beverage must fit the family budget.
2. **Nutritive value**: for example, milk and fruit juices give nutrients, while many soft drinks give only sugar.
3. **Age and health of the people**: children, the sick, diabetics and old people need different drinks (for example, little sugar and no stimulants for children).
4. **Occasion and weather**: a hot drink on a cold morning, a cold drink in hot weather, a drink to go with the meal or for a party.
5. **Quality and safety**: the packaging must be sealed and undamaged, the label (ingredients, expiry date) must be read, and the drink must be fresh and clean.
themes: beverages and drinks in the diet

questions.enonce_markdown:
List six (6) rules to follow when deep frying.

(6 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Six rules to follow when deep frying (1 mark each):

1. Use a **deep, strong pan** (or a deep fryer) with a flat base, and **fill it only about half full** of oil so that it does not overflow.
2. Use a **good frying oil** that can be heated to a high temperature without burning.
3. **Heat the oil until it is hot enough before adding the food**; food put into oil that is too cool becomes greasy.
4. **Dry the food** (or coat it with batter or breadcrumbs) and **do not overcrowd the pan**; fry in small batches so that the oil stays hot.
5. **Lower the food gently** with a basket or a slotted spoon, and never leave the hot oil unattended, to avoid splashes, burns and fire.
6. **Drain the fried food on absorbent paper**, and let the oil cool, strain it and store it covered after use.

(Other correct points: turn the pan handle away from the edge of the cooker, keep a lid nearby to smother a fire, and never pour water on burning oil.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Classify vegetables and give an example in each case.

(7 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Vegetables are classified according to the **part of the plant that is eaten**:

| Class | Part eaten | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Leaf vegetables | Leaves | Cabbage, lettuce, spinach |
| Root vegetables | Roots | Carrot, beetroot |
| Tubers | Swollen underground stems | Potato, yam, cocoyam |
| Stem vegetables | Stems | Celery, asparagus |
| Bulbs | Swollen leaf bases | Onion, leek |
| Flower vegetables | Flower heads | Cauliflower, broccoli |
| Fruit vegetables | Fruits | Tomato, cucumber, okra, eggplant |
| Seeds and pods | Seeds or pods | Peas, green beans, sweet corn |

(Any seven classes with a correct example earn the 7 marks.)
